PullRequest.Title: sessions: use Customizations icon for chat pill
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary - replace the bookmark glyph on the Agents Window Customizations pill with the same extensions icon used by the Agents Window navigation - add browser regression coverage for the rendered pill icon ## Screenshots | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ## Testing - `node .\test\unit\browser\index.js --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatInputPills.test.ts --browser chromium` (19 passing) - `npm run compile-client` *(blocked before compilation because the upstream `@github/copilot-sdk` tarball currently returns 404 from packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io)* cc @BenS

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Customizations status pill in an Agents Window session when customization entries are present and the pill is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable session sections are flattened, visibility is evaluated, and the pill view item creates one icon span using ThemeIcon.asCSSSelector. The changed option only substitutes Codicon.extensions for Codicon.bookmark on this existing synchronous render path; no additional prerequisite work is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of customization entries controls the existing section flattening and summary label, but the changed icon work remains one constant-time CSS selector/class substitution per rendered Customizations pill regardless of entry count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering runs synchronously on the UI thread under the existing observable/action-view-item lifecycle. The diff adds no queue, task, parallel operation, limiter interaction, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both codicons are statically registered ThemeIcon objects and require no runtime fetch or cache fill. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent for the changed path; there are no cache keys, misses, negative results, or coalescing concerns introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence. The changed production line replaces one static icon object with another, and the traced renderer converts either object to a CSS class on the same existing DOM span without new reads, boundaries, retained state, or repeated work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: exact paint cost is environment-dependent, but both values traverse the identical one-element class-based codicon render path, so the diff does not create a scaling or blocking mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The product behavior is a constant-cost glyph substitution; the added browser test performs bounded one-time DOM setup only during the test suite and does not affect production runtime.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the Customizations pill through source construction, visibility evaluation, action-view-item rendering, codicon registration, and the added browser test. No actionable performance regression or concrete regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
